about: The one hand-written input. For every conditional row it names the condition its guidance states, quoting the condition phrase verbatim from the row; gen_vectors.py refuses any quote it cannot find in the extracted cell. Every other designation is read straight from the Designation column. Ambiguities and observations each cite the table or clause and page where the text that raises them is printed, and quote it.

ambiguities.finding: The Description and Designation cells are transposed: the Description cell reads "Required" and the Designation cell holds the description. The schemas read the field as Required.

The pointer names a field that is not printed (1.7.3) and a field that is only conditionally recommended (1.7.1, Source URL). The table also prints no 1.4 and no 1.8, and the evident referents one step lower are 1.6.1 and 1.6.3, which are conditionally recommended in this table. No condition under which 1.6 is required can be read from the row, so the schemas carry no rule for 1.6 and list it as not machine-expressible.
The pointer names a field that is not printed. The evident referent is 1.7.1. The schemas carry no rule for 1.7 and list it as not machine-expressible.

Subfield 1.5.4 is conditionally required ("Required if the provider organization has planned or acted upon such a date"), but the parent's pointer names only 1.5.1 and 1.5.3. Clause 6 says a subfield's parent "shall be designated as required under at least the same set of circumstances", and also allows a requirement to be "conditioned on the parent field being populated". When a decommissioning date is planned, the dataset is not accessible outside the provider, and 1.5 is absent, the two readings disagree. No member sits in that case; the schemas apply the row as printed.

ambiguities.quote: Required if the provider organization has planned or acted upon such a date; otherwise optional.
ambiguities.finding: The same gap as A4 one table later: 1.6.4 is conditionally required and its parent 1.6 has no condition that can be read (A2). No member sits in the case where a decommissioning date is planned and 1.6 is absent.

Data Enhancement is Optional while its subfields 4.8.1 and 4.8.1.1 are Recommended and 4.8.2 and 4.8.3 are Conditionally recommended. Clause 6 says the parent of a recommended subfield "shall be designated as recommended or required under at least the same set of circumstances", unless the recommendation is "conditioned on the parent field being populated", which the rows do not say. The schemas apply each subfield's recommendation only where 4.8 is present; no member sits in a case where 4.8 is absent and the readings disagree.

ambiguities.quote: Recommended even if 5.1.1 is not populated.
ambiguities.finding: 5.1 is recommended without condition while its parent 5 is conditionally required ("See 5.1 and 5.3.") and carries no recommendation otherwise. Under the Clause 6 convention for recommended subfields this is the same gap as A6, at the recommended level. The schemas apply the recommendation where 5 is present.

ambiguities.quote: Recommended if the model can be accessed by entities outside the provider organization; otherwise optional.
ambiguities.finding: 1.6.1 and 1.6.3 are conditionally recommended under a parent (1.6) whose condition cannot be read (A2), and 1.7.1 is conditionally recommended under a parent (1.7) whose condition cannot be read (A3). The schemas apply each recommendation where its parent is present. In Table A.2.1 the matching fields 1.5.1 and 1.5.3 are conditionally required, not recommended.

ambiguities.quote: Fields 5.1-(*) and 6.1-(*) in Table A.3.1 are meant to refer to datasets.
ambiguities.finding: Table A.3.1 prints the dataset references as 5.2-(*) and 6.1.1-(*); there is no 5.1-(*) or 6.1-(*). The same paragraph says these fields "shall document the datasets using the default dataset documentation profile given in A.2" and that its requirements "may be relaxed", so the schemas do not apply the A.2 profile inside them and list the sentence as not machine-expressible.

The condition names "Use Rights and Restrictions"; the field is printed as "Usage Rights and Restrictions" (root field 3). The declared condition attribution-mandated is read as referring to root field 3.

ambiguities.finding: The only row with this designation, which Clause 6 does not define as a separate designation. It is read as a requirement conditioned on the parent being populated, which Clause 6 permits, and its condition is read from the number of 6.5-(*) entries (see the row's reading).
